teaser: Stratechery is launching a new feature for subscribers: The Daily Update, as a podcast. Now you can read or listen to every post on Stratechery.

title: DOJ Public Workshop on Venture Capital and Antitrust
teaser: Video of Ben’s appearance on a panel for a Public Workshop on Venture Capital and Antitrust hosted by the Department of Justice

title: First, Do No Harm
teaser: As regulators look closer at acquisitions they should be extremely wary of unintended consequences. The current system works well for everyone, most of the time.

title: Brandless Closes, The DTC Facebook Challenge, DTC Versus Softbank
teaser: Brandless is closing down, which is being spun into a commentary on Softbank. This is fair, but the bigger takeaway is about DTC broadly.

title: The Corona Virus Whistleblowers; NBA Salary Cap Decreases; Apple, Benefits, and Risks
teaser: The Coronavirus continues to spread in China, even as reports emerge of why it was not dealt with in time to make a difference, reframing the costs of authoritarianism.

title: Spotify Earnings, Podcasts and Lifetime Value, The Ringer Acquisition
teaser: Spotify’s mixed earnings, why podcasts are uniquely valuable to the company, and where The Ringer fits in.

title: The Iowa Fiasco, The Best Feature, Three Lessons
teaser: The fiasco surround the Iowa caucuses is an occasion to learn three lessons: what is a tech company, technology is hard, and why Facebook is like Microsoft.

title: Google Earnings, YouTube and Google Cloud, Google’s Falling Margin
teaser: Google finally released new financial information about YouTube and Google Cloud, but it is still not sufficient. Then, Google’s margins are falling just like Facebook’s: is the engine finally sputtering?

title: Facebook’s Platform Opportunity
teaser: Facebook is under pressure from all sides, but that actually means it has an opportunity to build the platform it has always wanted — in digital ads.

title: Exponent Podcast: It’s Been a Week
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we eulogize Professor Clayton M. Christensen. Listen to it here.

title: Epic Systems and Electronic Health Records, Aggregators and Data Portability, Epic’s Privacy Objections
teaser: Epic Systems, an electronic health records company, is protesting a mandate that they make consumer health care available via API. Their arguments highlight the tension between interoperability and privacy.

title: Apple’s Earnings, Slowing Services Growth, Apple and the Coronavirus
teaser: Apple’s surging iPhone sales and slowing services growth suggest that lots of iPhone customers are upgrading. It’s a testament to how strong Apple’s position is that revenue it misses now it catches later.

title: The Tragic iPad
teaser: The iPad is 10, and while it remains a useful device, it is ultimately a disappointment. Apple lost the vision for what the iPad could be, and never gave space for developers to figure it out for them.

title: Clayton Christensen Passes Away, Professor Christensen and I, Kobe Bryant and Measuring Your Life
teaser: There is no greater influence on Stratechery than Professor Clayton Christensen, but it is another death — Kobe Bryant’s — that reminds me of what truly matters.

title: Netflix Earnings; Self-Production, Cash Flow, and Margin; Netflix’s New Rung
teaser: Netflix’s earnings were mostly more of the same, but management’s comments helped explain an interesting connection between cash flow and margin, and showed how Netflix has evolved again.

title: iCloud Backups and Encryption; Facts, Principles, and Concerns; Determining Defaults
teaser: More encryption news, this time about how Apple holds the keys to iCloud backups. I think this approach strikes the right balance: privacy exists, particularly if you work for it, while acknowledging legitimate societal concerns.

title: Clearview AI, The Problem with Scraping, Tradeoffs
teaser: Clearview AI is billed as a story about facial recognition, but the most important questions it raises is about scraping. And, by doing so, it reveals how many trade-offs we have yet to confront.

title: Exponent Podcast: The Water We Swim In
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The End of the Beginning. Listen to it here.

title: Lime Leaves 12 Cities; Scarcity Amongst Abundance; An Update on Apple, Trump, and Encryption
teaser: Scooter companies appear to be struggling, which is not a surprise; still, it is an excuse to re-visit assumptions around ride-sharing in comparison, and an generalizable principle about Aggregation Theory. Plus, an update on Apple versus the FBI.

title: Visa/Plaid Follow-Up; Apple v FBI, Round 2; 2020 Differences
teaser: More on Visa/Plaid, including why payments in the U.S. and China are so different. Then, Apple is facing off against the FBI again, but its position is both stronger technologically and weaker politically.

title: Visa, Plaid, Networks, and Jobs
teaser: The history of credit cards helps explain why Plaid is valuable to Visa, and how Visa can make it significantly better.

title: Casper Files for IPO, Casper’s Business, Spotify Ad Targeting
teaser: Casper is a tech-enabled company, but so are its many competitors. Trying to win with brand is difficult in a market defined by infrequent purchases. Spotify, meanwhile, is seeking to expand the podcasting market beyond companies like Casper.

title: CES Concepts, Verizon Drops Bundles, Technology and TV
teaser: CES is boring, because no one knows what is next. Then, Verizon is dropping Internet and TV bundles, which is a rational response to the changing nature of pay-TV. It also shows how much tech disruption is still to come.

title: The End of the Beginning Follow-Up, Technological Revolutions and Financial Capital, Venture versus Productive Capital
teaser: Examining The End of the Beginning through the lens of Carlota Perez’s Technological Revolutions and Financial Capital , and what that means for venture capital.

title: The End of the Beginning
teaser: The beginning of technology was about the shift from batched computing in one place to continuous computing everywhere. That era of paradigm changes may be over, which means the real changes are only beginning.

title: Bubble Talk, Revisited; It [Wasn’t] 1999; The Big Tech Basket
teaser: While 2015 Unicorns did not meet expectations, that doesn’t mean 2015 was a bubble. Indeed, the most surprising reality is how well established big tech companies did.

title: AB 5 and Health Care, Project Connected Home Over IP, Ecosystem Pragmatism
teaser: A more flexibility economy would benefit from a stronger safety net. Then, a new standard that actually has real potential. It’s a win for some companies, but questionable for others.

title: The 2019 Stratechery Year in Review
teaser: The most popular and most important posts on Stratechery in 2019.

title: SBNation and AB5, Understanding SB Nation, AB 5 and the Internet
teaser: SB Nation is a publishing company that was only ever possible because of the Internet. That it has to change its model because of AB 5 shows why AB 5 is fundamentally flawed.

title: Cisco Sells Chips, The Conservation of Attractive Networking, Twitter MoPub Revenue
teaser: Cisco is selling chips, which is a fascinating example of the Conservation of Attractive Profits. Then, Twitter’s MoPub revenue is more than it seems.

title: Bluesky, The Twitter Protocol Tragedy, Alternatives
teaser: Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey announced that the company would be setting up a team to pursue a more open alternative to social network; unfortunately, the time to do so was ten years ago.

title: TV Advertising Falls; The Sports Linchpin, Revisited; NBA Ratings
teaser: TV Advertising is down, as price increases finally overwhelm the decline in viewers. It’s important to note, though, that sports still matter. This is something the NBA may not completely understand.

title: Regulating Demand, Ad Targeting and Unintended Consequences, Expedia CEO Out
teaser: Google’s continued dominance may not be intransigence, but rather the difficulty of regulating demand. Then, how Apple helps Google and Facebook, and Barry Diller isn’t blaming Google.

title: A Framework for Regulating Competition on the Internet
teaser: Understanding the differences between platforms and Aggregators is critical when it comes to considering regulation.

title: AWS re:Invent; Transformations, Transitions, and Databases; Amazon Outposts
teaser: The AWS re:Invent keynote was quite compelling, as Amazon made the case for enterprises to not simply transition to the cloud but to transform their approach to IT — which, of course, favors Amazon.

title: Larry Page and Sergey Brin Step Down, Why Now?, Google Going Forward
teaser: Larry Page and Sergey Brin’s impact on Silicon Valley is incomparable; now, though, they are formalizing a departure that arguably happened years ago. Why now, and what should Alphabet and Google do next?

title: Portability and Interoperability
teaser: Data portability is friendly to consumers, but it has very little to do with encouraging competition, at least relative to interoperability.

title: Facebook Buys Beat Saber, Capital and Copyright, The Oculus Conundrum
teaser: Facebook has bought Beat Games, a company of the future, and not just because they made a game for VR. Then, why it is the old world that needs capital, and why Oculus is still confusing strategically.

title: Airbnb Losses, Airbnb and The Google Squeeze, Airbnb’s Marketing Spend
teaser: Airbnb is losing money, thanks to a big increase in marketing. It matters greatly what that marketing is for.

title: PayPal Acquires Honey, What Honey Is, PayPal’s Play
teaser: PayPal bought Honey, which is best known as a browser extension. What does this mean for both end users and merchants, and which is more important?

title: Exponent Podcast: More Ergonomic
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Integration and Monopoly. Listen to it here.

title: Trump Visits Mac Pro Factory, Apple’s Tariffs, Apple Versus GitHub
teaser: Trump visited the Mac Pro factory, and people are disappointed in Tim Cook. First off, tariffs are certainly the driving fact, but I am disappointed too, for different reasons than most.

title: Recode Recap: John Stankey of WarnerMedia, Kevin Mayer of Disney
teaser: Highlights from Recode Media interviews of Warner Media’s John Stankey and Disney’s Kevin Mayer, including an extended discussion on sports.

title: Integration and Monopoly Follow-Up, Apple Paternalism, TikTok and CFIUS
teaser: More on Apple and restrictions on competition, and why it is different than Google. Then, Apple’s actions around vaping cross the line, plus why TikTok does not deserve the benefit of the doubt.

title: Integration and Monopoly
teaser: Apple has won through integration, but integration combined with network effects and economies of scale can result in bad outcomes that look a lot like monopolies.

title: Facebook Pay, Google Checking, Tech Company Differences
teaser: Facebook announced Facebook Pay, which is far different from Libra. Then, Google is apparently getting into checking, which leads to a question of motivations: each of the tech companies are approaching financial services from a different angle.

title: The Google Squeeze Follow-up, Disney+ Launch, Instagram Influencer Follow-Up
teaser: Google’s approach to travel mirrors its approach to Shopping, which, correctly or not, was already ruled to be illegal in Europe. Then, Disney+ rolls out like a movie, and fails like a service. Plus, more on Instagram and influencers.

title: The Google Squeeze
teaser: Google, the real Aggregator, is squeezing OTAs, which acted like Aggregators while depending on Google for demand. It’s easy to say Google is being unfair, but this may be better for consumers.

title: Instagram to Hide Likes, Instagram and Influence Marketing, Practical Impacts
teaser: Instagram is removing likes, because it says it cares about user welfare. Is that the reason, or is Instagram finally taking on influencer marketing?

title: Exponent Podcast: Principle Stacks
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Tech and Liberty. Listen to it here.

title: Microsoft Ignite, Azure Arc, Additional Insight Announcements
teaser: Microsoft’s Ignite keynote and announcements show a company that is back to the same strategy it has always had, just one a new value chain.

title: Tech and Liberty Follow-up, Facebook Earnings, Additional Notes on Facebook Earnings
teaser: Making principled stands should not mean absolutism: Facebook should seek to ameliorate its trade-offs. Then, Facebook’s earnings continue to show higher costs, plus where Zuckerberg is right and wrong in defending the Instagram acquisition.

title: Tech and Liberty
teaser: The First Amendment is not about a law, but rather a culture — specifically a culture of liberty. It is essential to tech, and in this context, Facebook is mostly right about political ads (but can still do better).

title: Google Buys Fitbit, Why Fitbit is a Good Idea, Why It Isn’t
teaser: First some important updates about Stratechery, then Google is seeking to acquire Fitbit. Why the acquisition makes sense, and why it doesn’t.

title: Apple Earnings, iPhone Pricing, Additional Notes on Apple’s Earnings
teaser: Apple had another quarter where the iPhone didn’t dominate, plus more evidence that the company is thinking like a Services company.

title: HBO Max, AT&T’s Challenges, The Streaming Battleground
teaser: AT&T announced details about HBO Max, which are both safe and aggressive, and also raise questions about AT&T’s long-term stewardship. Then, why Netflix and Disney are the long-term winners.

title: Amazon Earnings, AWS Concerns, Google Earnings
teaser: Amazon’s earnings are encouraging because profits are down. Still, there is reason for concern around AWS. Then, Google’s top-line continues to impress, but the company continues to waste huge amounts of money, hurting the bottom line.

title: Microsoft Wins JEDI Contract, Microsoft Versus Amazon, Microsoft Earnings
teaser: Microsoft won the JEDI contract with the Department of Defense under questionable circumstances, which shouldn’t disguise the fact that Microsoft had a compelling case. Then, Microsoft’s earnings are impressive but too vague.

title: Exponent Podcast: The Second Estate Era
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Internet and the Third Estate. Listen to it here.

title: SoftBank Rescues WeWork, Owning WeWork, Zuckerberg in Congress
teaser: SoftBank is rescuing WeWork in a very strange transaction, then re-visiting what I have written about WeWork. Plus, Zuckerberg’s appearance in Congress confirmed why Libra is the wrong approach for the company.

title: Ghost 3.0, An Interview with Ghost CEO John O’Nolan
teaser: There is a new offering in the subscription space: Ghost. John O’Nolan, the founder and CEO of the Ghost Foundation, explains what makes Ghost unique.

title: Zuckerberg’s Speech, Facebook Versus China, The Structure of Free Expression
teaser: Digging into the specifics of Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s speech, particularly the company’s role in a contest of values with China, and why free expression depends on more than good intensions.

title: The Internet and the Third Estate
teaser: Mark Zuckerberg suggested that social media is a “Fifth Estate”; in fact, social media is a means by which the Third Estate — commoners — can seize political power. Here history matters.

title: Ambient Computing and Antitrust, Google’s New Revenue Streams, Netflix Earnings
teaser: The real antitrust concern is with potential constraints on ambient computing. Then, Google has its own Services Narrative, and Netflix’s earnings should be viewed with concern.

title: Google and Ambient Computing
teaser: Google presented a vision of ambient computing that goes beyond the smartphone. The company is well-placed, but faces challenges both in the marketplace and in the mirror.

title: Exponent Podcast: The Abyss Stares Back
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The China Cultural Clash. Listen to it here.

title: Libra Launches, Loses Members; A Note on Facebook v Warren; The Office of Emerging Technologies
teaser: Libra launches, but may be dead before it begins. Then, Facebook v Warren is a reminder of the value of the U.S. approach — and an indirect way to explain how silly San Francisco is.

title: Apple Pulls Hong Kong App, Tim Cook’s Memo, Honesty and Control
teaser: It was Apple’s turn to be in the spotlight in China; what was surprising was how unprepared the company seemed to be. Then, why companies dealing with China, including Apple, should be more honest.

title: China Cultural Clash Follow-Up, Disney and Blizzard, Choosing Customers
teaser: More on TikTok, then Disney and Blizzard demonstrate how expensive customers can be, while Google and Facebook benefit.

title: The China Cultural Clash
teaser: The NBA controversy in China highlights a culture clash that both tech companies and the U.S. government need to take to heart. Plus, why Tiktok being Chinese is increasingly a problem.

title: Apple App Store Changes, Google to Remove French News Excerpts, Europe Bans Content Worldwide
teaser: Apple is softening App Store lock-in by the barest amount possible. Then, Google shows its power in France, but a case against Facebook shows how limited that power is.

title: Exponent Podcast: Distracted at Facebook
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Facebook from multiple angles, including child sexual abuse material, encryption, Oculus, and a leaked all-hands meeting. Listen to it here.

title: Microsoft’s Surface Event, Victors and History, Microsoft’s Hardware Prospects
teaser: Microsoft (eventually) selling a phone that runs Android is not particularly meaningful in terms of its impact financially but is a totem of a major shift culturally.

title: Facebook’s All-Hands Leak, Facebook Versus Warren, Zuckerberg’s Culture
teaser: The most newsworthy aspect of Facebook All-Hands leak is what its existence says about Facebook itself. What is most interesting, though, are not the comments about Elizabeth Warren but what Mark Zuckerberg showed about himself.

title: Beachheads and Obstacles
teaser: Facebook and Amazon had events on the same day for Oculus and Alexa. Both are driven by lessons from the mobile era, but Amazon seems to have learned more than Facebook.

title: Child Sexual Abuse Material Online, The Problem With Community, Towards More Friction
teaser: A horrifying article on Child Sexual Abuse Material online is actually a sign that Facebook is doing the right thing, at least for now. Encrypting private communications, though, may make things worse.

title: Neither and New Follow-Up, Adam Neumann Forced Out, Peloton IPOs
teaser: Why Neither/New companies are different than traditional marketplaces, how Vision Fund’s flaws led to Adam Neumann being forced out, and why Peloton has a big opportunity it might not see.

title: Neither, and New: Lessons from Uber and Vision Fund
teaser: Uber represents something new: a company that is different than incumbents because of technology, yet not itself a tech company — just like the Venture Fund is not a VC.

title: Facebook Acquires CTRL-Labs, Acquisitions and Value, The Portal and Facebook’s Reputation
teaser: Facebook is acquiring CTRL-Labs, a computer-neural interface that is potentially a great fit with Oculus. At this point, though, is Facebook’s involvement in this new technology value-destructive?

title: Exponent Podcast: The Exponent IPO
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Cloudflare and what it is like going through an IPO, as well as what has gone wrong with WeWork. Listen to it here.

title: Peacock and Flex, Seinfeld to Netflix, Big Bang Theory and HBO
teaser: Updates on TV streaming, including Peacock, Flex, Seinfeld, Netflix, Big Bang Theory, and HBO.

title: WeWork Delays IPO, Datadog Prices IPO, SoftBank and Going Big
teaser: WeWork abandons its IPO, for now, and is likely at the mercy of Softbank. Then, why Datadog is set to have a great IPO, in direct counter to WeWork and a direct rebuke to Softbank’s approach.

title: Day Two to One Day
teaser: Amazon.com was showing signs of being a Day Two company, including the alleged manipulation of search. There is reason, though, to be optimistic that the company has gotten back to Day One. Plus, where are the other big tech companies?

title: AB 5, Uber, and the Gig Economy; The ABC Test; What Comes Next
teaser: California has passed a new bill, AB 5, that may have a big impact on Uber, Lyft, and other similar companies, but only if it survives court and ballot challenges. The unintended consequences could be huge.

title: The Apple Watch Tells Time, Additional Observations on Apple’s Event, Revisiting App Store Search
teaser: The “Always-on” Apple Watch update is an important one, additional notes from Apple’s event, and why the company is likely being honest about App Store Search

title: The iPhone and Apple’s Services Strategy
teaser: Apple’s annual iPhone event may have marked Apple’s true shift into being a Services company

title: App Store Search, WeWork to Shelve IPO?, The Vision Fund Wobbles
teaser: The New York Times has a compelling expose of how Apple dominates App Store search. Then, WeWork may not IPO, although its CEO will be fine; the bigger question, though is about SoftBank’s Vision Fund.

title: Apple Versus Project Zero, Apple’s Poor Response, The China Paradox
teaser: Apple took on Google’s Project Zero over the weekend, and didn’t come out looking particularly good, particularly since China is a huge paradox for Apple.

title: Slack Earnings, Slack’s Sales Cycle, The FTC Fines YouTube
teaser: Slack’s earnings were fine, but lacked the explosive growth their valuation needed. Understanding Slack’s past and future product-market fit explains why. Then, the real problem with the FTC’s fine of YouTube is a lack of transparency.

title: Tech Companies and Hardware, The Cost of Low Margins
teaser: Software-differentiated hardware companies are tech companies, but be careful about low margins leading to a destructive cycle where marketing costs drown a company.

title: What Is a Tech Company?
teaser: The question of “What is a tech company” comes down to how much software and its unique characteristics affects the company’s core business.

title: Apple Updates Siri Policy, The Missed Middle Way, Alexa and Automobiles
teaser: Apple has updated its Siri policy, but misses a middle way on privacy that Amazon gets right. Then, Alexa has an opening in cars, but probably not for long.

title: Privacy Fundamentalism Follow-up, Peloton’s S-1, Peloton and Disruption
teaser: Answering two criticisms of Privacy Fundamentalism , and then looking at Peloton’s S-1 and answering the question as to whether or not they are a tech company through the lens of disruption.

title: Privacy Fundamentalism
teaser: The current privacy debate is making things worse by not considering trade-offs, the inherent nature of digital, or the far bigger problems that come with digitizing the offline world.

title: Trump Orders Companies to Look for China Alternative, Apple’s Chokepoint, The Potential Tariff Impact
teaser: Apple’s risk in the trade war is becoming very real, with tariffs set to hit the end of this week. Tim Cook continues to leverage his relationship with President Trump, but that is only a temporary solution to a single chokepoint on the company’s business.

title: Apple Card Launches, Without a Website; Revisiting Stratechery: If Steve Ballmer Ran Apple
teaser: Apple Card launched without a website, which suggests something fundamental about Apple’s nature. Then, revisiting a Stratechery article from six years ago.

title: Why WeWork Isn’t AWS and the CEO Problem, Cloudflare’s S-1, Contrasting S-1s
teaser: The comparison of WeWork to AWS shouldn’t be taken too far, because software is different. Look no further than Cloudflare’s IPO. Plus, leadership matters.

title: The WeWork IPO
teaser: The WeWork IPO is defined by audaciousness and excess, all of which is driven by unlimited access to capital.

title: Verizon Sells Tumblr to Automattic, What Went Wrong?, Tumblr’s Future
teaser: Verizon is selling Tumblr to WordPress for only $3 million. Why did Tumblr fail, and is there reason for optimism with Automattic as its new owner?

title: Disney’s Bundle, Huawei’s HarmonyOS, Uber Earnings
teaser: Disney’s bundle is compelling both for Disney and also Hulu, then Huawei’s new OS doesn’t make sense commercially but does make sense geopolitically. Plus, Uber’s earnings have been unfairly represented even as they are very concerning.

title: Why Cloudflare Matters, The Absence of Gatekeepers, Promotion Versus Moderation
teaser: More on moderation, including why Cloudflare is important systematically, a reminder that there are no more gatekeepers, which means moderation is always reactive, and why Facebook and YouTube still deserve the most scrutiny.

title: A Framework for Moderation
teaser: The question of what should be moderated, and when, is an increasingly frequent one in tech. There is no bright line, but there are ways to get closer to an answer.

title: 8chan and El Paso, Cloudflare Drops 8chan, An Interview with Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince
teaser: Cloudflare dropped 8chan as a customer after this weekend’s shootings; CEO Matthew Prince explains the company’s thought process, the responsibilities of infrastructure providers, and what a sustainable Internet looks like.

title: The Athletic Reaches 500,000 Subscribers, Brute-Forcing the Bundle, Local Bundles
teaser: The Athletic has 500,000 subscribers and continues to pursue growth over profitability. It’s an approach that makes sense, and the demise of local bundles helps explain why.

title: Revisiting Google’s Cloud Numbers, Apple Earnings, Additional Notes on Apple Earnings
teaser: Google’s cloud numbers are probably much worse than they appear. Then Apple delivered post-iPhone earnings that were impressive in what they said about Apple’s future.

title: Uber Layoffs, T-Mobile-Sprint Merger Approved, Additional Notes on the Merger
teaser: Uber’s layoffs were a necessary adjustment to a marketing strategy that made sense previously, but not today. Then, why the T-Mobile-Sprint merger should have been approved, and the secondary impacts of the decision.

title: Google Earnings, Amazon Earnings
teaser: Google’s earnings came with the usual dearth of information, although it appears that Google Cloud is growing more than expected. AWS growth, meanwhile, is definitely slowing as Amazon’s business broadly is running out of low-hanging fruit.

title: Facebook’s FTC Settlement, Assigning Blame, Facebook Earnings
teaser: The FTC has released its complaint against Facebook, leading me to change my mind and put more blame on the company. Complaints about the FTC are still misplaced, though: the real problem is Congress. Meanwhile, Facebook continues growing undeterred.

title: Snap Earnings, Notes and Concerns, DoorDash and Tipping
teaser: Snap’s earnings were impressive, including the most valuable AR application of all time, but the company still needs to show it can earn advertisers broadly. Then, DoorDash responds to pressure from the demand side.

title: Tinder Bypasses Google Play Payments, App Store Fees and Differences, Apple Entering Modem Business?
teaser: Tinder is moving away from Google Play Store’s payment system, which makes sense given the app’s pricing power. Then, how the app store tax warps costs, and why Apple may not see much upside from getting into modems.

title: Microsoft Earnings, Teams Passes Slack, The Partner Advantage
teaser: Microsoft continues to crush earnings with its integrated approach. Then, Teams passed Slack, and its lead will likely widen, because it is a sustaining technology, not a disruptive one. Plus, the importance of Microsoft partners.

title: Libra in Congress; Global Community, Revisited; Messianic Versus Money-Making
teaser: Libra had a chilly reception at Capitol Hill, which highlighted a fundamental tension between Internet companies and lawmakers. Then, why it was inevitable that Facebook would make Libra, and why it was probably the wrong choice.

title: Netflix Earnings; Reasons for Concern, and Optimism; Apple Reportedly Pursuing Exclusive Podcasts
teaser: Netflix’s earnings are worrisome, but for predictable reasons; ultimately, the company remains in a strong position. Then, Apple’s rumored move into exclusive podcasts doesn’t make sense and is in fact good for Spotify.

title: Substack Raises Series A, An Interview With Substack Co-Founders Christopher Best and Hamish McKenzie
teaser: An interview with Substack Co-Founders Christopher Best and Hamish McKenzie, who recently raised a Series A to enable newsletters from Andreessen Horowitz.

title: Facebook’s FTC Fine, Apple and Microsoft’s Mistake, IBM’s Unbundling
teaser: Facebook’s FTC fine is being pilloried, but it really is large and unprecedented. Plus, why Facebook critics were asleep at the wheel. Then, Microsoft saving Apple has an analogy to IBM, and is a potential argument in favor of antitrust action.

title: Shopify Follow-up, Defining Definitions, OpenDoor Partners with Redfin
teaser: More on Shopify, including why I was reluctant to cover the previously, but now see the promise of the Internet in their model. Then, why I’m excited about being uncertain, and how Redfin and Opendoor’s partnership helps define the market in home-buying.

title: Shopify and the Power of Platforms
teaser: It is all but impossible to beat an Aggregator head-on, as Walmart is trying to do with Amazon. The solution instead is to build a platform like Shopify.

title: HBO Max and Friends; British Airways, Marriott Hit with GDPR Fines; Zoom’s Vulnerability
teaser: HBO Max is AT&T’s new streaming service, and it is paying a lot for Friends. Then, the best part of GDPR has its intended effect, while Zoom shows that security still isn’t a priority

title: Walmart’s E-Commerce Struggles, Textbook Disruption, The Benefits of Not Competing
teaser: Walmart is struggling in ecommerce for very predictable reasons; the company — and economy — is better off leveraging its assets and not competing directly with Amazon.

title: Netflix Loses The Office, Netflix’s Budget Consciousness, Spotify Ends Direct Uploads
teaser: It is hard to see *The Office* being a good deal for NBCUniversal, even if Netflix will miss it. Then, Netflix’s budget consciousness is just as likely to be a sign of Netflix power than it is weakness, and more reasons why Spotify isn’t Netflix.

title: Apple, Design, and Operations; So It Goes; The Role of Jeff Williams
teaser: More on Jony Ive’s exit, and why blaming Tim Cook misses the broader changes that are an inevitable by-product of success. Than, clarifying Jeff Williams role as CEO-in-waiting.

title: [FREE] Jony Ive Leaves Apple, Ive’s Legacy, The Post-Ive Apple
teaser: Jony Ive is leaving Apple: how it happened, Ive’s legacy, and what it means for Apple going forward.

title: Libra’s Questionable Benefits, Facebook’s Hidden Costs, Philosophical Objections
teaser: While Facebook, Libra, and the Long Game was about analysis, this Daily Update is about opinion: I don’t think Libra is a good idea.

title: An Interview with Kevin Weil and Dante Disparte About Libra and Calibra
teaser: An interview with Kevin Weil, the VP of Product at Calibra, and Dante Disparte, the Head of Policy and Communications at the Libra Association, about Libra and Calibra.

title: Facebook, Libra, and the Long Game
teaser: Libra is less about an immediate benefit to Facebook, and more about creating a world where companies like Facebook have the best chance to prosper. That is why Facebook gave up so much control.

title: Exponent Podcast: Game of Phones
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Apple’s Audacity. Listen to it here.

title: The New Dropbox, The Cloud OS, Connecting Versus File-Sharing
teaser: The New Dropbox is making a bid to be the Cloud OS, something only Microsoft has pursued. It took Dropbox a long time to realize the opportunity, but better late than never.

title: Delrahim’s Speech on Tech and Antitrust; Tech and Antitrust, Updated; YouTube and Instagram’s Scale Defense
teaser: The Department of Justice antitrust chief gave a speech yesterday that should make tech nervous, particularly Google and Facebook. Then, why Google and Facebook’s scale defense is not sufficient.

title: Tech and Antitrust Follow-up, Google Buys Looker, Salesforce Buys Tableau
teaser: Sometimes analysis is about what will happen, not what should happen. Then, two big acquisitions in the data analytics face: Google’s purchase of Looker makes sense, while Salesforce is paying a steep price for Tableau.

title: Tech and Antitrust
teaser: A review of the potential antitrust cases against Google, Apple, Facebook, and Amazon suggests that only Google is vulnerable.

title: Cloudera and Pivotal, Box and Zuora

title: China’s Alleged Hardware Hack, How the Attack (Allegedly) Happened, Believability and Implications
teaser: Bloomberg has published an explosive report alleging a hardware hack that has affected multiple companies, including Apple and Amazon; both deny it. What might have happened, who can be believed, and what might happen next?

title: Data Factories Follow-Up, Amazon’s Pay Raise, Amazon Makes Hay
teaser: Follow-up to Data Factories , then Amazon’s pay raise, which is of course good for workers and also, unsurprisingly, good for Amazon.

title: Data Factories
teaser: Facebook and Google and other advertising businesses are data factories, and regulation will be most effective if it lets users look inside

title: Microsoft Ignite, Weaknesses To Strengths, Amazon’s Device Announcements
teaser: Microsoft’s Ignite conference was another reminder that the company no longer focuses on the consumer, a point Satya Nadella emphasized as a strength. Then, Amazon helps explain why.

title: WhatsApp Founder Speaks, EU Deception?, Facebook Ideology
teaser: More Facebook drama, this time from an interview with WhatsApp co-founder Brian Acton. What was most noteworthy, though was the response.

title: Six Years of Systrom, Instagram’s Alternate Reality, Facebook’s Red Flag
teaser: Despite this week’s bad news, Facebook won with Systrom’s tenure. Then, what might have been with an independent Instagram, and the worrying signals this sends about Facebook the app.

title: Instagram’s CEO
teaser: The surprising resignation of Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger should not, in fact, be surprising: this became inevitable the moment they sold Instagram to Facebook.

title: New Alexa Devices, Amazon and the EU Commission
teaser: Why is Amazon selling more Alexa devices? More broadly, do the company’s house brands leave it susceptible to an antitrust challenge?

title: The iPhone XR Delay, India, and China; Discriminatory Job Ads on Facebook; EU Versus Internet Follow-Up
teaser: More follow-up on the iPhone, then how discriminatory job ads on Facebook demonstrate how to police bad behavior on platforms with zero marginal costs. Plus, follow-up on The European Union Versus the Internet .

title: The European Union Versus the Internet
teaser: The EU is back to regulating tech companies, and getting the Internet wrong in the process. That, though, helps illuminate an approach that could work.

title: iPhone Classes; iPhone Growth Drivers, and Limiters; The Apple Watch
teaser: Will the iPhone XS slump like the iPhone 6S? Probably not, because theories about the iPhone 6S slump are probably wrong. Plus, the Apple Watch.

title: The iPhone Franchise
teaser: The iPhone is a franchise, a product that will make money in well-defined ways; Apple understands that and is exploiting it more than ever before with the iPhones XS and XR.

title: Apple’s iPhone Event, Facebook Fact-Checking, Vimeo Pivots Again
teaser: A preview of Apple’s iPhone event, a revelatory controversy about Facebook fact-checking, and yet another pivot by Vimeo thanks to mistakes made years ago

title: Strengths, Weaknesses, and Augustus; Zuckerberg’s Blindspot; The Liberal Arts Fallacy
teaser: The New Yorker is out with a huge profile of Mark Zuckerberg and Facebook; what does the article get right, what is the real problem with Facebook, and where do critics go wrong?

title: Spotify and the Labels, Labels and Aggregation, Newspapers and Texture
teaser: Spotify and the labels are at odds, largely because the latter don’t understand their competitive environment. Then, Apple is trying to build the news bundle.

title: Sandberg and Dorsey in Congress, Dorsey and Incentives, Google’s Absence
teaser: Facebook’s Sheryl Sandberg and Twitter’s Jack Dorsey testified in front of Congress; the former had the most to lose, while the latter hinted at exactly what.

title: Xbox All Access Pass, The Eighth-Generation of Consoles, Console Subscriptions: Now and the Future
teaser: Microsoft is announcing a new subscription plan for Xbox that includes the console; it is modest for now, but could be a bigger deal in the future.

title: San Francisco and Scooters, Skip’s Strategic Moat, Santa Monica and Scooters
teaser: San Francisco has decreed which scooters should win, and acquiesce to regulators appears to be top of the list. Plus, why the differences between scooters and ride-sharing should result in very different strategies.

title: AMD and Modularity Follow-Up, Trump and Tech, Tech’s Vulnerability
teaser: The problem with AMD’s modularity approach; then, Trump attacks tech. The claims are baseless but that hardly means the industry is in the clear.

title: Uber Follow-up; GlobalFoundries Abandons 7nm; Pricing Power, Differentiation, and Integration
teaser: Not all of Uber’s efforts are new, but the urgency is. Then, there are only three foundries pursuing 7nm, which means more pricing power (and how this applies to Uber and self-driving cars).

title: Uber’s Bundles
teaser: Uber had a good strategy, but its crisis meant Lyft had new life and the strategy was no longer workable. Now the company is pursuing something new, even though it is more complicated.

title: Fortnite’s Bad Bug, Epic’s Complaint, The Downside of Open
teaser: Fortnite has a bad bug, and while the company is being blamed for circumventing the Play Store, Android’s design is a big part of the problem.

title: Fortnite Skips Google Play, Netflix Explores Bypassing iTunes, Big Names and Long Tails
teaser: Fortnite is skipping out on Google Play, and Netflix is trying to get out of the App Store. That’s not great for Apple and Google, but the effort is hardly a surprise.

title: Facebook, Germany, and Filter Bubbles; The Nutella Factor; Facebook’s Response
teaser: A new study suggests that Facebook is to blame for increased attacks on refugees in Germany. The data isn’t perfect, but the worries about filter bubbles should be taken seriously.

title: Disney and the Resilient Cable Bundle, Disney’s Streaming Plans, ESPN+ and Serie A
teaser: Disney has had a difficult three years, particularly from a stock perspective, but things aren’t as bad as feared, and there is a strategy for the future.

title: Tencent’s Profit Drops, China Freezes Game Approvals, The Tencent Behemoth
teaser: Tencent’s profit dropped, in part because the Chinese government has stopped approving games. Plus, why Tencent’s approach to the games industry makes sense in China, even if Facebook’s model may be more attractive.

title: Facebook Stories Follow-up, Twitter and Newton’s Third Law
teaser: History suggests that Stories will be an advertising success; then, the Alex Jones episode shows how un-monopoly-like social networks are.

title: Facebook’s Story Problem — and Opportunity
teaser: Snapchat is losing users, and it seems clear the biggest reason is Instagram Stories: that is a win for Facebook, but the pain in advertising may be substantial.

title: MoviePass, Finally; Value Chains and Unit Costs; Atlassian and Slack
teaser: Finally, the MoviePass breakdown so many have been asking for; then, another story to catch-up on, about Atlassian, Slack, and leadership.

title: Uber Loses in New York City, The Modern Medallion?, Driver Pay Floors
teaser: New York City has enacted a moratorium and pay floor on ride-sharing services. Uber may be losing its political power, and the effects could be wide-ranging.

title: Free Daily Update: An Interview with Patreon CEO Jack Conte and Memberful CEO Drew Strojny
teaser: An interview with Patreon CEO Jack Conte and Memberful CEO Drew Strojny on the occasion of Patreon acquiring Memberful, the membership software used by Stratechery. This Daily Update is free for everyone.

title: Patreon Acquires Memberful, An Interview with Patreon CEO Jack Conte and Memberful CEO Drew Strojny
teaser: An interview with Patreon CEO Jack Conte and Memberful CEO Drew Strojny on the occasion of Patreon acquiring Memberful, the membership software used by Stratechery. This Daily Update is free for everyone.

title: Sonos’ IPO, The De-Integration of Sonos, Spotify Earnings
teaser: Sonos will begin trading today, but it faces a tough road without meaningful integration. Spotify faces a difficult road too: it is interesting to think about what they would look like together (even though it won’t happen).

title: Apple Earnings, ASP and “New” iPhones, Steve Jobs and the App Store
teaser: Apple’s earnings not only held true to form, but actually had an upside surprise in ASP. Plus, what an interview with Steve Jobs reveals about differentiation and integration.

title: Android-EU Follow-Up, Google Earnings, Facebook and the Stock Market
teaser: Follow-up on Google’s EU decision, and a reminder that Google really good for consumers. Then, Google’s strong quarterly results, and why the understanding Facebook’s strategic advantages may be divorces from their stock price.

title: Facebook Lenses
teaser: Facebook was down dramatically after its last earnings; to decide if it is justified it is worth looking at the company through many different lenses, both financial and strategic.

title: The European Commission Versus Android
teaser: Examining the history of Android explains why the European Commission may be right to fine Google for its actions around Android, even as the reasoning feels off.

title: Another Congressional Hearing, The Genesis of Section 230, The Battle over Section 230
teaser: Section 230, which shields Internet companies from liability, is getting more attention: the only attention it should get is as a model for other regulations.

title: Netflix Earnings, Netflix’s Rising CAC, Content and Marketing
teaser: Netflix’s subscriber numbers were disappointing; does the company have a customer acquisition cost problem? Then again, customer acquisition costs should include content, which might not have been good enough.

title: Amazon Switches?, AWS Versus Azure, Photoshop on iPad
teaser: Amazon’s rumored move into Switches is being framed as being about Cisco, but I suspect it’s about Microsoft. Then, Adobe is making Photoshop for iPad, which benefits from subscriptions.

title: The Apple Espionage Case, Apple’s New Organization, The App Store Turns 10
teaser: A corporate espionage case involving Apple gives clues about Project Titan. Better news is Apple’s new organization. Plus, the App Store turns 10 and Apple won’t change its approach there.

title: Uber Invests in Lime, Uber Versus Google Maps, AT&T and HBO
teaser: Uber is investing in Lime along with Google: is the real competition between Uber and Google Maps? Then, AT&T is considering big changes for HBO — or are they?

title: Xiaomi IPOs, Samsung’s Profit Slips, The Smiling Curve
teaser: Xiaomi’s IPO shows a company that has come full circle but still has a long ways to go. Then, Samsung remains reliant on components for profit, and both companies show that the Smiling Curve applies to smartphones more than ever.

title: Facebook Filter Foibles, The EU Copyright Directive, Yelp and the Three Approaches to Internet Content
teaser: Facebook provides a useful example of how automated filtering goes wrong, even as the E.U. mandates exactly that. A recent court case about Yelp shows that the U.S. has the best approach to content law.

title: Apple’s Map Reset; CarPlay, Waze, and Google Maps; Disney Acquisition of 21st Century Fox Approved
teaser: Apple Maps is getting a reset; what is more encouraging is the company inviting competition. Then, Disney gets approval for its purchase of 21st Century Fox, and it raises questions about the entire process.

title: Twitter Reorganizes, Twitter Turnaround?, Twitter and the Extremes
teaser: Twitter is reorganizing the company, and it’s probably a good sign. Meanwhile, has the company made a turnaround? The product — and company — is inevitable high variance.

title: Amazon Acquires PillPack, PillPack’s Alignment With Amazon, The Walmart Miss
teaser: Amazon’s acquisition of PillPack makes a lot of sense for both companies, and it’s hard to argue that consumers won’t be the ultimate beneficiaries.

title: South Dakota v. Wayfair, and Amazon; Wayfair’s Unintended Consequences; Ohio v. American Express, and Tech
teaser: Two Supreme Court decisions have an impact on tech: first, states can collect sales taxes on e-commerce, and second, the burden of proof for antitrust just got higher.

title: Instagram Launches IGTV, IGTV’s Monetization, YouTube Channel Memberships
teaser: Instagram’s launch of IGTV was impressive because of the clear thinking behind it; the long-term question, though, is about monetization, both for the service and for creators, something YouTube is good at.

title: Intel and the Danger of Integration
teaser: Intel is in an increasingly bad position in part because it has been captive to its integrated model. Or, you could simply say they were disrupted.

title: Disney Ups Bid for 21st Century Fox, Disney’s Choice, AT&T to Acquire AppNexus?
teaser: The AT&T-Time Warner decision that I has set off a chain reaction with an uncertain ending: Comcast and Disney are competing for 21st Century Fox, and AT&T may be getting into digital advertising.

title: Microsoft and ICE; Tech and Trump, Revisited; Lines and Responsibilities
teaser: Microsoft is facing both internal and external pushback for its contract with ICE in the light of the Trump administration decision to separate families at the border; it is time for tech executives to decide where the line is between rhetoric and action.

title: Apple, China, and Trump; Google Invests in JD; The Value of the China Market
teaser: More on Apple’s challenges in the Chinese market, both in the past and going forward, and then why e-commerce companies are beating everyone else, both in China and the U.S. Then, why the China market is so attractive.

title: AT&T, Time Warner, and the Need for Neutrality
teaser: It is no surprise that a judge allowed the AT&T-Time Warner acquisition to proceed given the government’s poor case; the question is if a better case could have been made. What is ultimately needed, though, are new laws.

title: Scooter Follow-up, Microsoft and the Xbox, Spotify Signs Indie Acts
teaser: Scooter follow-up, then why the future of gaming may be very good for Microsoft. Plus, why Spotify’s new distribution agreements are not a big deal for now, but point to a positive future.

title: The Scooter Economy
teaser: Scooters are everywhere, and the use case is amazing. What is not so clear, though, is how scooter companies can build strong businesses, which means consumers are the real winners.

title: Exponent Podcast: Legacy Leverage
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Cost of Developers. Listen to it here. Note: This is the last episode of the season; Exponent will return in the fall

title: Morris Chang Retires; Apple, Microsoft, Facebook Follow-Up; Who Gets to Be on the Steam Store?
teaser: Morris Change, the founder of TSMC, is one of the most important tech figures in history. Then, follow-up on Microsoft-GitHub, Apple and the App Store, and Facebook and the New York Times. Plus, why Valve is getting platform control right.

title: Apple Centricity, Watch Tentposts, Apple’s Philosophy and Managing Time
teaser: An overview of the WWDC keynote, including Apple’s transition away from touch, how the Apple Watch is reaching its potential, and why Apple’s approach to screen time is so refreshing.

title: The Cost of Developers
teaser: Microsoft paid a lot for GitHub, because it had to pay directly for access to developers. It doesn’t have the leverage of users the way that Apple does on the App Store.

title: Microsoft to Buy GitHub, A Win for GitHub, Facebook’s Data-Sharing Deals with Device Makers
teaser: Microsoft is reportedly buying GitHub, which makes a lot of sense for both Microsoft and GitHub, and all GitHub users. Then, why the latest Facebook scandal is probably overblown.

title: Internet Trends: Smartphones and Internet Usage, Tech’s Takeover, The Small Business Revolution, Tech’s Deflationary Effect
teaser: The slides that stood out to me from Mary Meeker’s annual Internet Trends report.

title: Snap’s Monetization Flaw; Microsoft and the Effect of Antitrust; Apple, Russia, and Telegram
teaser: Reactions from the Code Conference interviews with Snap CEO Evan Spiegel and Microsoft President and Chief Legal Officer Brad Smith, plus a very problematic demand of Apple by the Russian government.

title: The Bill Gates Line Follow-up, Twitter and the Bill Gates Line, Data Portability and Facebook
teaser: Following up on The Bill Gates Line , applying it to Twitter, and then why Facebook portability is a bad idea.

title: Exponent Podcast: Black Holes
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Bill Gates Line. Listen to it here.

title: Okta’s Developer Conference, An Interview with Okta CEO Todd McKinnon
teaser: An interview with Okta CEO Todd McKinnon on the occasion of the company’s developer conference.

title: The Bill Gates Line
teaser: Understanding the differences between aggregators and platforms matters for companies interacting with them and also regulators considering antitrust.

title: Adobe Buys Magento, Podcast News, ZTE Deal Reportedly Reached
teaser: Adobe reached the logical endpoint of its digital ad build-out, but was the journey worth it? Then, news from the podcast world, and the potential resolution of the ZTE ban.

title: Sports Gambling Defederalized, Amazon Channels
teaser: Sports gambling is defederalized, and the opportunity is likely larger than people think: then, Amazon Channels is another manifestation of the company’s “first customer” strategy.

title: Exponent Podcast: Platforms Versus Aggregators
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Moat Map. Listen to it here.

title: Spotify’s New Hate Policy, Twitter’s Behavior Policy, YouTube Music and YouTube Premium
teaser: Spotify’s new hate policy and Twitter’s behavior policy seem like good things at first glance, but what they suggest about the companies’s power is worrisome. Plus, YouTube’s subscription plans are as confusing as ever.

title: The Moat Map Follow-up; Uber, YouTube, and Spotify; The Public Cloud and Scale
teaser: More on The Moat Map , and how it applies to Uber, YouTube, Spotify and the public cloud.

title: The Moat Map
teaser: The Moat Map describes the correlation between the degree of supplier differentiation and the externalization (or internalization) of a company’s network effect.

title: ZTE and Trump, Dropbox Earnings, Bloomberg’s Paywall
teaser: The ZTE saga takes a twist, Dropbox’s first earnings are solid, and Bloomberg shows how the rich get richer.

title: Exponent Podcast: Two By Twos
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Tech’s Two Philosophies. Listen to it here.

title: Platforms Versus Aggregators, What About Amazon?, Walmart Buys Flipkart
teaser: Tech’s two philosophies are also about the difference between platforms and aggregators, but even that has its own divisions. Amazon falls on both sides of the divide. Plus, why Walmart’s Flipkart purchase makes no sense.

title: Tech’s Two Philosophies
teaser: Google and Facebook represent one philosophy, and Microsoft and Apple represent another; tech needs both, but ultimately platforms are more important than aggregators.

title: Microsoft’s Build Keynote, Microsoft and IBM, Microsoft’s Realism
teaser: Microsoft’s Build keynote didn’t garner much attention, because there was nothing for consumers: that is exactly what made it so compelling.

title: Spotify Earnings, Spotify’s Free Plan and Hulu Partnership, Snap Earnings
teaser: Spotify’s earnings were not what the market expected, but the company gained credibility. Snap, meanwhile, doesn’t have any credibility at all.

title: Exponent Podcast: Round Numbers
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Divine Discontent: Disruption’s Antidote. Listen to it here.

title: Apple Earnings, Facebook’s F8 Keynote, Facebook Dating
teaser: Apple’s earnings were less interesting than the expectations game. Facebook’s F8 conference, meanwhile, again cast Zuckerberg’s vision of technology in stark contrast to Steve Jobs. Plus, why Facebook Dating will likely flop.

title: Divine Discontent: Disruption’s Antidote
teaser: Apple has long defeated disruption by focusing on the user experience; Jeff Bezos and Amazon, though, show that user expectations for their experience are ever-changing.

title: Softbank and Sprint, Amazon Earnings, Jeff Bezos’s Letter and Interview
teaser: Sprint and the problem of fixed costs, Amazon and the advantage of fixed costs, and Jeff Bezos’ fundamental optimism

title: T-Mobile to Acquire Sprint, Microsoft Earnings
teaser: T-Mobile is acquiring Sprint. The deal makes a lot of sense, particularly in the context of 5G — will regulators look forward or backward? Then, Microsoft continues to own the CIO relationship.

title: Exponent Podcast: Zillow and Sustaining Aggregation
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Zillow, Aggregation, and Integration. Listen to it here.

title: Open, Closed, and Privacy Follow-Up; Facebook Earnings; Notes on Facebook Earnings
teaser: A follow-up to Open, Closed, and Privacy , then multiple notes on Facebook’s earnings: the company’s executives sounded confident, and they should be.

title: Open, Closed, and Privacy
teaser: Just as encryption is only viable on closed systems, so it is that increased privacy regulations will only entrench walled gardens. That should affect thinking on regulation.

title: Google Earnings, Google’s Cost Drivers, Other Bets Versus Google Ventures
teaser: Google’s Earnings show rapidly rising expenses, which makes sense as the company seeks to grow outside of its core competency. Plus, why even Google is often better off investing instead of expanding.

title: Google’s Messaging Announcement, Allo’s Go-to-Market Problem, Chat: The Open Alternative
teaser: Google’s announced Chat , which is not a new messaging service but the adoption of a new messaging protocol to replace SMS. It’s not an ideal outcome, but the only possible one.

title: Netflix Earnings and the Video Value Chain, The Conditions of Aggregation, Comcast and Netflix and the New Bundle
teaser: Netflix’s earnings are a reminder of the power that comes from not just aggregation but also integration. It also reveals that Aggregators are more likely to gain economic power when suppliers are already modularized. Plus, Netflix and Comcast start to build the new bundle.

title: The ZTE Ban, Tech’s Trade War Risk, China’s Delayed Approval and Apple’s Pain
teaser: The U.S. government banned companies from selling to ZTE for issues unrelated to the current trade war; that may not much matter, and Apple and other U.S. tech companies could soon feel the pain.

title: Zillow, Aggregation, and Integration
teaser: Zillow fits the description of an aggregator, but it hasn’t transformed its industry due to a lack of integration. Now it is trying to do exactly that.

title: Exponent Podcast: Facebook Fatigue
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Facebook Current. Listen to it here.

title: Zuckerberg’s House Hearing, Toutiao’s Apology, Apple’s Siri Hire
teaser: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg was back on the hill, using his usual talking points; the contrast with a Chinese news app, facing its own political pressure, was striking. Plus, why Apple’s Siri hire is so important.

title: The Facebook Current
teaser: The Senate hearing about Facebook was a bigger deal than it might have seemed, both because it happened and because of what was said.

title: Uber Acquires JUMP, Background on Bikes, Uber’s New Strategy?
teaser: Uber has acquired JUMP, the dockless e-bike company. It’s an acquisition that makes sense for both sides, and suggests that Uber has a more coherent strategy than previously.

title: Technologists, Politics, and Facebook; Publishers and the GDPR; Facebook and The Denver Post
teaser: Publishers are in ever more trouble, thanks to the GDPR. It increasingly seems like Facebook and Google are the inevitable saviors, for better or worse.

title: Exponent Podcast: There’s Always a Bigger Fish
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The End of Windows. Listen to it here.

title: Mark Zuckerberg’s Press Conference, The Bosworth Memo, The Facebook Data Lockdown
teaser: Mark Zuckerberg blamed The Pollyannish Assumption for his mistakes, but an internal memo suggested that Facebook may have misunderstood itself. Then, the walls around the company’s garden grow stronger.

title: Spotify Debuts; Trump, Amazon, and the USPS; The Politics of Amazon
teaser: Spotify debuts, and I really want to be bullish, but it’s hard. Then, Trump might have a point about Amazon, but it’s moot: the company should be defended.

title: The End of Windows and Slack Versus Microsoft Teams, ARM on Macs?, Apple’s Commitment to the Mac
teaser: Microsoft Teams is another example where Windows held too much sway. Then, ARM might be coming to the Mac; if it is, it shows the importance of commitment.

title: The End of Windows
teaser: The Windows division no longer exists at Microsoft, marking the end to a four-year process of changing Microsoft’s culture.

title: Uber Sells Out in Southeast Asia; Uber’s Self-Driving Tragedy; Doing the Right Thing, Inevitably
teaser: Uber is officially out of Southeast Asia, ultimately thanks to Softbank. Then, tragedy, as an Uber self-driving car kills a woman. This may be the end of the program, but the decision should have been made before.

title: Stratechery 4.0 Follow-up, Apple’s Educational Event, The Meaning of Better
teaser: A quick aside as to why Stratechery doesn’t have an app, then a review of Apple’s educational event, and why the company’s business model limits it in education relative to Google.

title: Stratechery 4.0
teaser: The newest version of Stratechery.com: now explore the site via concept, company, or topic, or use dramatically improved search functionality. Plus, a new logo!

title: Five Years, Facebook’s Apology, Facebook’s New Scandal
teaser: First, a reminder that social media has big benefits, before diving back in to Facebook’s burgeoning scandal; it seems clear the company doesn’t understand exactly what it is facing.

title: Exponent Podcast: Facebook’s Real Mistake
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Facebook Brand. Listen to it here.

title: Salesforce Acquires Mulesoft, The Enterprise Cloud Opportunity, Salesforce’s Opportunity
teaser: Salesforce is acquiring Mulesoft. While the price seems high, there is a unique opportunity to be the integration layer in enterprise software.

title: What Was Facebook Thinking?, Facebook’s Platform Folly, Does This Mean Regulation?
teaser: The answer to “What Was Facebook Thinking” may be less about strategy and more about not understanding the type of company Facebook was meant to be. Plus, why regulation probably isn’t imminent.

title: The Difference Between Google and Facebook, Facebook’s Pedantry, Facebook and the Value of Data
teaser: More on the fallout from Facebook and Cambridge Analytica: why Google and Facebook are different, why that explains how they treat data, and why Facebook seems so oblivious.

title: The Facebook Brand
teaser: The Facebook brand is, due to Facebook’s strategic choices, about not respecting privacy. That is why the Cambridge Analytica story is such a problem for the company.

title: Exponent Podcast: Qualcomm, Patents, and Innovation
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Qualcomm, National Security, and Patents. Listen to it here.

title: Drake on Twitch, Fortnite vs PUBG and Selling Feelings, The Returns to the Best
teaser: Drake was playing video games on Twitch, and it blew up: there is so much to unpack about games, new business models, Twitch, and asymmetrical returns on the Internet. (Plus, a brief note on that Siri article)

title: Apple Acquires Texture; The Problem with Magazines; Texture, Apple News, and Bundles
teaser: Apple acquired Texture and is taking the last, best shot at building a digital text bundle.

title: Qualcomm, National Security, and Patents
teaser: The Trump administration blocked Broadcom’s acquisition of Qualcomm, and I think it was the right move. Understanding why means understanding Qualcomm and Broadcom’s plan for the company — and the problem with patents.

title: Google Sells Zagat to The Infatuation, The Infatuation and Zagat, More on Google and AMP
teaser: A review of why Google bought Zagat, what The Infatuation might do with the review site, and the parallels with the AMP project.

title: Exponent Podcast: 90’s Alt Forever
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss Lessons From Spotify. Listen to it here.

title: The Athletic Raises $20 Million, Four Stories on Tech and Politics
teaser: The Athletic is right to go for it, and raise more VC money. Then, tech and politics is only becoming more complicated as national security concerns enter the debate.

title: More Spotify; Spotify, Uber, and Airbnb; Uber, Waymo, and SoftBank
teaser: A bit more on Spotify, and then the lessons to be learned by Uber and Spotify. Plus, a potential Uber-Waymo partnership, and why they company will likely sell-out in Southeast Asia.

title: Could Spotify Be Netflix?, Calculating Spotify’s LTV and CAC
teaser: Spotify is in a much weaker position that Netflix was, because it could not build up a user base before negotiating with its suppliers. However, the company does seem to be acquiring customers efficiently.

title: Lessons From Spotify
teaser: Spotify has a marginal cost problem, but while the cause is unique to Spotify, the challenges are more applicable than it seems.

title: Exponent Podcast: Dilly-Dallying Dropbox
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Dropbox Comp. Listen to it here.

title: Ring, Alarm.com, and Bottom-up Ecosystem Building; Dropbox and Timing; Apple, China, Microsoft, the United States
teaser: More follow-up on both Ring/Amazon and Dropbox, then why Apple in China explains why the Supreme Court should rule in favor or tech companies.

title: Amazon Buys Ring, Ring’s Exit, Amazon’s Strategy and the Integration of the Home
teaser: Amazon is buying Ring: it makes sense for the latter to sell, and while the reasons for the former to buy are less obvious, they are equally compelling.

title: Dropbox’s Cost of Revenue, Cost of Revenue and Churn, Cloudy Dropbox
teaser: Dropbox’s falling cost of revenue has received a lot of attention, but absent more data, the trend appears unsustainable — just a company getting ready to go public.

title: The Dropbox Comp
teaser: Dropbox has filed its S-1, but comparisons with Box, Atlassian, and Slack demonstrate how difficult it is to tell just how good its business is.

teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we discuss The Aggregator Paradox. Listen to it here.

title: More on Chrome and AMP, The Case Against Google, Decentralization and Paradigm Shifts
teaser: More on Chrome and AMP, and what The Case Against Google gets wrong about Microsoft. Then, why decentralized networks are aggregator kryptonite.

title: The Aggregator Paradox
teaser: Google is winning with AMP and blocking ads in Chrome: both seem bad, but aren’t they actually good for consumers? That is the paradox of aggregation.

title: The Mueller Indictment, Russian Sophistication, Facebook Tweets
teaser: The Mueller investigation produced its first indictment, and the biggest takeaway was the degree of Russian sophistication. This was good news for Facebook, until an executive undid it all.

title: Exponent Podcast: The Mailbag Episode
teaser: On Exponent, the weekly podcast I host with James Allworth, we answered reader questions. Topics include business school, career advice, the nature of strategy, creating the next Silicon Valley, and how governments should deal with the disruptions caused by the Internet. Listen to it here.

title: Olympics Ratings, P&G and Olympics Advertising, Total Audience Advertising
teaser: Olympic Ratings are down, but less than expected! Unfortunately for NBC, so is revenue. That, though, is expected: sports and its advertisers remain interconnected. Then, at least NBC finally figured out how to manage multiple mediums.

title: Twitter Earnings; The End of TellApart; Direct Versus Brand Marketing, and Size
